title: The Local Group
objective: After this level you can describe the small group of galaxies the Milky Way belongs to.
summary: The Milky Way is one of about 100 or more galaxies in the Local Group, dominated by us and Andromeda, about 10 million light-years across.

cards.headline: Our galaxy lives in a neighborhood.
The neighborhood
cards.body: The Milky Way belongs to the Local Group, a gathering of about 100 or more galaxies about 10 million light-years across. Two big spirals dominate it: the Milky Way and Andromeda. Most of the rest are small dwarf galaxies.

cards.headline: Our satellites
cards.body: The Large and Small Magellanic Clouds are small galaxies orbiting the Milky Way. From the Southern Hemisphere they’re visible to the naked eye as two faint, cloudy patches of light.

cards.fact: Andromeda is the Local Group’s other giant.
cards.context: From a dark site you can spot it with the naked eye as a faint smudge, even though it lies about 2.5 million light-years away.

cards.headline: Local Group: mapped
learned: The Milky Way belongs to the Local Group
It has about 100 or more galaxies
The Milky Way and Andromeda dominate it
The Magellanic Clouds orbit our galaxy

questions.prompt: Which two galaxies dominate the Local Group?

options.label: Andromeda and M87
options.rationale: M87 is far outside the Local Group.

questions.explanation: The Milky Way and Andromeda are the two big spirals that dominate the Local Group.

questions.prompt: Where can you see the Magellanic Clouds with the naked eye?

options.label: From anywhere on Earth
options.rationale: They’re in the far southern sky.

questions.explanation: The Magellanic Clouds sit in the southern sky and are visible to the naked eye from the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.prompt: From Level 81: what type of galaxy are the Magellanic Clouds?
questions.explanation: The Large and Small Magellanic Clouds are irregular galaxies, with no clear shape.
